Neon has premiered a new poster for Luca Guadagnino’s “Artificial,” which is far cleverer than you might suspect.

On the surface, it appears to be a generative AI work, complete with a few key mistakes that often come with ChatGPT’s tech – from a bridge that’s half sunk to mismatched lighting.

When initially launched this morning, a bunch of people immediately criticised it as pure AI slop – and that’s the gag.

Look closer, and you’ll see a detailed canvas very much made by a human, specifically artist Mike Thompson along with marketing agency Gravillis Inc. Neon has, in fact, shared a video showcasing the one-sheet’s creation and how it’s filled with lots of little easter eggs.

The result has gotten people talking about the film, which looks into the meteoric rise of OpenAI – the company behind ChatGPT – along with the personal rivalries, ego clashes, and ethical tensions behind the scenes.

The cast includes Andrew Garfield as current CEO Sam Altman, Yura Borisov as machine learning engineer Ilya Sutskever, and Ike Barinholtz as Elon Musk along with Monica Barbaro, Cooper Hoffman, Zosia Mamet, Chris O’Dowd, Cooper Koch, Billie Lourd, Jason Schwartzman and Mark Rylance.

“Artificial” opens in select cinemas on December 25th before expanding nationwide on January 8th.
